lesson_title: Three Sectors in One Loaf of Bread
hook_text: Every loaf of bread you buy has passed through all three sectors of the economy.
clip_script: Follow a loaf of bread backwards. The corner shop sold it to you: selling is a service, that is the tertiary sector. A truck delivered it: transport, tertiary again. A bakery baked it from flour, water and yeast: making something new, that is the secondary sector. A mill ground the wheat into flour: secondary too. And a farmer grew the wheat in a field: taking straight from nature, that is the primary sector. Take from nature: primary. Make: secondary. Serve and sell: tertiary. Your school shoes did the same: cattle on a farm, a leather and shoe factory, then a shop. One question sorts any business: what does it mainly do? And here is the surprise. In South Africa, about two-thirds of everything we produce comes from services. Most of the jobs of the future are in the tertiary sector.
visual_style: A loaf of bread rewinding through a shop, a delivery truck, a bakery oven, a mill and a golden wheat field, with three coloured sector labels stamping onto each stage.
pacing: A smooth rewind montage, a crisp three-word rule, a surprising statistic to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort every business on your street into its sector.
